original_question: Consider a p-cyclic cover X_K -> P^1_K of genus g = (p - 1)(m - 1)/2. For a fixed degeneration type, there is an upper bound on the order of the wild automorphism group of the special fiber. Can the wild monodromy group Gal(L/K)_w be maximal for that degeneration type, meaning that it attains this upper bound?
target_in_paper: Question 6.17 in Section 6.2.1 ("The wild monodromy") of the Lehr-Matignon contribution "Automorphisms of curves and stable reduction": "For a given type of degeneration can the wild monodromy group Gal(L/K)_w be maximal (in the sense of attaining this bound)?"
correct_elements: Your draft captures the right target very closely: it keeps the p-cyclic cover over P^1, the genus parameterization g=(p-1)(m-1)/2, the dependence on a fixed degeneration type, the existence of an upper bound coming from automorphisms of the special fiber, and the central question of whether the wild monodromy Gal(L/K)_w can be maximal by attaining that bound. That is essentially the content of Question 6.17.
missing_details: The paper's local setting should be stated: K is taken in the mixed-characteristic p-adic/stably-reducing setup of Section 6.2.1; the authors then paraphrase the question specifically over Q_p^tame.
L/K should be defined as the minimal finite Galois extension over which X_K acquires semi-stable/stable reduction; this is the finite monodromy extension.
Gal(L/K)_w should be defined explicitly as the p-Sylow subgroup of the finite monodromy group Gal(L/K), following Definition 6.14.
The special fiber X_k should be identified as the special fiber of the stable model X of X_L.
The comparison is motivated by the faithful action Gal(L/K) -> Aut_k(X_k), which should be mentioned when making the question stand-alone.

The quantifier is existential: for a prescribed degeneration type, does there exist a p-cyclic cover with that degeneration type whose wild monodromy is maximal? The paper is not asking whether every cover of that type is maximal.
To be fully paper-faithful, "maximal" should be tied to the upper bound on the wild automorphism group/p-part of Aut_k(X_k) associated with the chosen degeneration type, rather than left informal.

The authors' own reformulation says they are looking for a p-cyclic cover of P^1 over Q_p^tame that degenerates to the given type and whose wild monodromy is as large as possible; that reformulation should be incorporated if one wants the question to read like the paper.
refined_question: Let K be in the mixed-characteristic local setting of Section 6.2.1 (equivalently, in the authors' reformulation, take K=Q_p^tame), and let X_K -> P^1_K be a p-cyclic cover of genus g=((p-1)(m-1))/2. Let L/K be the minimal finite Galois extension over which X_K has stable reduction, let X be the stable model of X_L, let X_k be its special fiber, and let Gal(L/K)_w be the p-Sylow subgroup of the finite monodromy group Gal(L/K). For a prescribed type of degeneration of the stable reduction of X_K, for which previous work gives an upper bound on the size of the wild automorphism group (equivalently, the p-part of Aut_k(X_k)) of the special fiber, does there exist such a p-cyclic cover with that degeneration type for which Gal(L/K)_w is maximal, i.e. attains that upper bound?
equivalent_formulation: Find a p-cyclic cover of the projective line over Q_p^tame that degenerates to a prescribed type and whose wild monodromy group Gal(L/K)_w is as large as possible, i.e. realizes the upper bound attached to that degeneration type.
justification: The draft is a near-paraphrase of Question 6.17. The nearby context first sets up the finite monodromy extension L/K, the faithful action Gal(L/K) -> Aut_k(X_k), and Definition 6.14 of the wild monodromy group Gal(L/K)_w. Immediately after that, the paper asks exactly whether, for genus g=(p-1)(m-1)/2 and a fixed degeneration type, the wild monodromy can be maximal by attaining the relevant bound on automorphisms of the special fiber. The following paragraph explicitly restates the same problem as finding a p-cyclic cover of P^1 over Q_p^tame with prescribed degeneration type and wild monodromy as large as possible; it also notes that the authors had already proved this for p=2 and m=5 (genus 2).
